contour.name: Разрешения, лицензии и разрешённая деятельность
contour.scope: Разрешение уполномоченного лица, предмет, территория, условия и срок. Коммерческое entitlement и IP grant сопоставляются, но не сливаются.
specific_questions: Как отличить разрешение регулятора от программной лицензии?
Как описать деятельность без кода классификатора?
Как фиксировать отзыв, приостановку и ограничения?
proposed_invariants: Разрешение не расширяется на дочерние компании автоматически
contour.negative_case: Наличие отраслевого кода в регистрации считается лицензией.
contour.acceptance_scenario: Проверить лицензию на одну площадку, временную приостановку и новый вид деятельности без разрешения.
comparison_tracks: OASIS UBL/FIBO: соглашения, стороны и обязательства
ODRL: разрешение, запрет, обязанность и ограничение
Первичные юридические источники выбранных юрисдикций; обязательна предметная проверка применимости

vercy_candidates.note: Связь требует проверки полного семантического crosswalk; published не означает завершённую независимую экспертизу.

blocking_decisions: Установить границу и решение reuse/extend/new по действующим спецификациям.
Подтвердить semantic crosswalk, права и source mastership.
Выбрать immutable refs; провести проверки fixtures до заявления о публикационной готовности.

model.name: Permit / Authorization
model.purpose: Represent the governed application, assessment and decision case for regulated authorization while keeping the permission-bearing grant in its authoritative external master.
model.scope_statement: Owns authorization-case identity, requested class and scope, submissions, evidence-use assertions, completeness, criterion assessments, consultations, decisions, reasons, notifications, appeal routes and follow-on administration cases. Applicants, authorities, legal instruments, public-service definitions, reusable criteria, evidence artifacts, payments, inspections, enforcement, appeals and granted rights remain external masters.
in_scope: Case identity, class, actors in procedural roles, service, legal basis and requested authorization scope
Application revisions, evidence-use, completeness, assessment, consultation, decision, reasons and notification
Follow-on renewal, variation, suspension or termination cases, access views, retention, interoperability and safe operations
out_of_scope: Permission-bearing permit, licence, authorization, credential or right master and its independently verified current status
Applicant, authority, legal instrument, public service, criterion, evidence artifact, payment, inspection, enforcement and appeal-case masters
Universal licensing law, legal advice or automated final decision without competent authority

boundary_notes.distinction: A favorable decision points to a separately mastered permission-bearing grant; case completion and grant validity are never interchangeable.
The reusable service definition supplies channels, requirements, outputs and legal resources; this model owns one execution case.
Reusable requirements and evidence artifacts keep external masters; the case owns submissions, supported claims, verification and assessment findings.
Inspections and enforcement actions may trigger or inform a case but retain their own authority, evidence and lifecycle.
Legal sources establish competence, requirements and effects; the authorization case applies them but does not own or reinterpret the law.

functions.name: Open authorization case
functions.description: Create case identity, class, authority, service, legal basis, applicant roles and requested scope.
preconditions: competence, identity and service version validate
effects: case becomes resolvable without creating a grant

functions.name: Submit application revision
functions.description: Append signed declarations, requested scope, receipt and completeness context.
preconditions: representation and required fields validate
effects: immutable revision is recorded for review

functions.name: Attach and verify evidence
functions.description: Link external evidence or registry data to requirements and record a verification assertion.
preconditions: purpose, provider and validity resolve
effects: evidence use stays attributable and privacy-scoped

functions.name: Assess criterion
functions.description: Record method, evidence used, result, reasons, uncertainty and accountable reviewer for one criterion.
preconditions: criterion and reviewer authority resolve
effects: finding contributes to review without becoming the final decision

functions.name: Request information or consultation
functions.description: Issue a cure, referral, consultation or inspection request and track the response deadline.
preconditions: authority, necessity and disclosure validate
effects: review is paused or enriched with attributable input

functions.name: Issue reasoned decision
functions.description: Record grant, refusal, partial, defer, withdrawal, lapse or closure with authority, reasons and effect time.
preconditions: competence, due process, reasons and affected scope validate
effects: case outcome is fixed without itself creating a grant master

functions.name: Notify and bind grant reference
functions.description: Record decision delivery, publication, appeal route and any separately mastered authorization identifier.
preconditions: decision, recipient policy and external grant resolve
effects: parties can verify outcome without conflating case and grant

functions.name: Open follow-on administration case
functions.description: Create renewal, variation, transfer, suspension, revocation, annulment, surrender or reinstatement case.
preconditions: grant and jurisdictional identity-continuity rule resolve
effects: later action stays auditable and cannot mutate grant by inference

functions.name: Issue purpose-bound case view
functions.description: Create applicant, regulator, public, statistical or sector exchange projection with declared omissions.
preconditions: access, freshness and target version validate
effects: view links source digest, scope warning and omissions

functions.name: Close and retain case
functions.description: Close, lapse, withdraw, archive or tombstone the case while preserving decisions, appeals and grant references.
preconditions: appeal, legal hold and disposition authority validate
effects: active processing ends while citable history remains

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint authorization-case identifiers only when no competent authority identity exists; keep applicants, authorities, legal sources, public services, criteria, evidence artifacts, payments, inspections, appeals, enforcement and grants as typed references.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by competent-authority case identifier and register, never by applicant, permit number, requested activity, decision date, document or hash.
Keep authorization case, application revision, assessment, decision, notification and external permission-bearing grant separately identifiable.
patch_rules: Extensions declare jurisdiction and sector profile, target finding, legal source, authority, criterion and exchange-profile versions and interoperability impact.
Case identity, competence, requirement semantics, decision effect or grant-reference changes require a successor revision, migration map and retained cited history.
compatibility_rules: Unknown additive fields may be ignored only when identity, competence, requested scope, criteria, evidence links, reasons, legal times, appeal, access and provenance remain intact.
Every CPSV, CCCEV, LegalRuleML or sector projection pins versions and states transformed fields, omissions and round-trip limits.

identity_priority: Competent authority's master case identifier, qualified by register and jurisdiction.
Governed globally resolvable authorization-case IRI with authority binding.
Dimension UUID or ULID when no external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and offset or Z; separate submission, receipt, assessment, decision, notification, legal-effect, observation, knowledge and ingestion times.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {authorization-case-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use applicant, permit number, title, date or hash alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, issuer, legal-source and profile versions, authority, source anchors, valid and knowledge times, quality, confidentiality, licence and access marking.

policies: Only a competent authority may issue a decision or establish its legal effect; automation may validate and recommend but cannot invent competence.
A successful process, payment, submitted evidence, status page or decision copy never alone proves a current external grant.
Criteria, evidence, inspections, enforcement and appeal records remain in their authoritative masters and are referenced with purpose and freshness.
Agents may perform reversible clerical actions and propose findings; final decisions, adverse actions, sensitive disclosure and disposition require accountable authority.

read: Resolve Dimension, jurisdiction, case register, competent authority, service and requirement versions, current revision, legal time and access purpose.
create: Create case identity, class, authority, legal basis, applicant roles, requested scope and explicit unknowns before assessment or decision.
update: Append submission, evidence-use, finding, consultation, decision or event with actor, authority, reason, time and provenance; never overwrite cited history.
delete: Apply appeal, legal hold and records policy; prefer withdrawal, closure or tombstone and never cascade to applicants, evidence, grants or enforcement records.

checklist.notes: Authority-qualified case identity is separated from application revisions, decisions and external grants.
Permit, licence, approval, registration, exemption and certificate classes are jurisdiction-qualified.
Requested scope, submissions, criteria, findings, decisions, reasons, deadlines and case states are first-class.
Receipts, evidence-use, verification, assessment, signature and notification evidence are covered.
Open, submit, verify, assess, consult, decide, notify, review, project and close operations are governed.
Parties, authorities, services, laws, criteria, evidence, payments, inspections, enforcement, appeals and grants retain external masters.
Submission, cure, review, decision, notification, follow-on action, closure and retention preserve history.
Actor roles, requirement-evidence links, consultations, decisions, appeals and grant references are typed.
Submission, receipt, assessment, decision, notification, effect, observation and knowledge times remain distinct.
Requested place and territorial jurisdiction are referenced without importing geographic masters.
Application derivation, evidence use, assessment method, decision authority and publication remain attributable.
Authorization case, rights register, evidence, payment, inspection and enforcement masters remain separate.
Identity, competence, completeness, criteria, evidence, reasons, legal time, appeal, access and stale-head checks are explicit.
Applicant, regulator, public, statistical and sector views are purpose-bound.
Submissions, findings, decisions, appeals, external grant links and tombstones are preserved.
CPSV-AP, CCCEV, LegalRuleML and UN/CEFACT sector projections are loss-aware.

known_omissions: No independent Claude or Grok result was available; later administrative-law and sector review is required before canonical promotion.

Certified CPSV-AP, CCCEV, LegalRuleML and sector-message crosswalks and conformance fixtures remain future work.
conflicts: The legacy model owns the application-to-decision process, while the permission-bearing grant remains an external right or attestation master.
Application status and current grant status can disagree and must not be inferred from one another.
Permit, licence, approval, registration, exemption and certificate classifications vary by jurisdiction and sector.
regional_assumptions: CPSV-AP, CCCEV and the Single Digital Gateway provide European interoperability patterns rather than universal administrative law.
UN/CEFACT FLAP is a fishing-sector profile and cannot define every permit process.
LegalRuleML represents legal and deontic semantics but does not create authority or a binding decision.
adversarial_checks: Reject a case identified solely by applicant, permit number, requested activity, date or file hash.
Reject a successful workflow, payment or evidence submission represented as a valid external grant.
Reject an automated recommendation treated as a competent authority decision.
Reject revocation, suspension, renewal or transfer inferred from monitoring without authoritative event and grant update.
Reject public verification that exposes protected case data or omits jurisdiction, scope, freshness and grant-master source.

model.name: Attestation / Credential
model.purpose: Represent issuer-asserted claims with durable identity, evidence, validity, status, securing and purpose-bound presentation while remaining independent of storage and interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns credential class and issued-instance identity, claim and schema references, issuer, subject and holder role bindings, issuance evidence, validity, status and lifecycle, secured representations, credential-specific verification evidence, presentations, disclosure manifests, interoperability mappings and governed retention. Party identity, issuer mandate, subject profile, source evidence, keys, permission-bearing grants, trust policy, authorization decisions and generic audit logs remain external.
in_scope: Credential and attestation definitions, instance and representation identity, typed claims, schema, vocabulary, issuer authority reference, subject binding and issuance evidence
Validity and terms, status method and freshness, suspension, revocation, expiry, renewal, correction, supersession, secured representations and verification results
Presentation requests, disclosures, holder binding, privacy and correlation, format mappings, role views, access, retention, provenance and safe agent operations
out_of_scope: Person, organization, issuer, subject, holder, verifier, mandate, source evidence, key, trust policy, permit grant, authorization decision or audit-log master lifecycle
Implementing proof, signature, wallet, PKI path, status-list or presentation-protocol algorithms and storing private keys or undisclosed secrets
Universal claim truth, issuer trust, identity proofing, authentication, authorization, eligibility, legal effect or certified cross-format equivalence

boundary_notes.distinction: The credential owns the issuer's claim expression and references evidence; source observations and evidence artifacts keep their own identity and provenance.
Issuer, subject, holder and verifier identities and public key references remain external; credential verification is not authentication by itself.
A licence or permit credential may evidence an external grant, but its authenticity and status do not themselves make an authorization decision.
Generic proof artifacts and verification methods remain external or reusable mixins; this model binds them to credential claim, validity, status and presentation context.
This model records credential-specific presentations and verification evidence, while wallet inventory and generic append-only audit execution remain external.

functions.name: Define credential class and profile
functions.description: Establish claim vocabulary, schema, required evidence, issuer authority, validity, status and representation rules.
preconditions: namespace, semantic definitions, issuer mandate, privacy and interoperability validate
effects: a versioned class is available without issuing an instance

functions.name: Issue attestation or credential
functions.description: Create an immutable issued assertion and representations after an authorized evidence-backed decision.
outputs: issued credential revision and issuance event
preconditions: issuer authority, subject binding, schema, evidence, validity, status method and expected serial validate
effects: issuer record and permitted holder copy are created with provenance

functions.name: Deliver, accept and custody holder copy
functions.description: Transfer a representation to a holder or wallet and record receipt without transferring issuer authority.
preconditions: holder authority, channel, integrity, privacy and recovery policy validate
effects: a controlled copy becomes available to the holder

functions.name: Publish or refresh status
functions.description: Issue a privacy-aware, time-qualified credential status assertion or list update.
preconditions: authority, method, purpose, index, freshness, signing and privacy validate
effects: relying parties can obtain current source-qualified standing

functions.name: Suspend, reinstate, revoke, expire, renew or supersede
functions.description: Append a credential lifecycle event and derived state while preserving earlier claims and representations.
preconditions: transition guard, authority, effective time, status publication, notification and lineage validate
effects: current standing changes without rewriting issued history

functions.name: Create presentation request
functions.description: Record verifier, purpose, audience, requested claims or predicates, formats, nonce and expiry.
preconditions: verifier identity, authority, minimization, client binding, nonce and expiry validate
effects: a bounded disclosure request becomes attributable

functions.name: Derive and present credential
functions.description: Create a request-bound presentation with permitted disclosure and optional holder binding.
preconditions: credential status, request, nonce, audience, holder binding, minimization and format validate
effects: the verifier receives purpose-bound evidence without mutating the credentials

functions.name: Verify credential or presentation
functions.description: Record schema, proof, key, path, status, time and request-binding checks and structured outcome.
preconditions: algorithms, canonicalization, keys, status freshness, time, trust input and policy version validate
effects: technical outcome becomes attributable without making an authorization decision

functions.name: Project or transform loss-aware
functions.description: Map a credential to another representation or sector profile with explicit omissions and semantic conflicts.
preconditions: source and target versions, issuer, subject, claims, validity, proof, status and round-trip class validate
effects: consumer receives a traceable representation with visible limitations

functions.name: Correct, retain, dispose and audit
functions.description: Create a successor correction or execute authorized retention and disposition while preserving required lineage.
preconditions: expected head, issuer authority, legal hold, subject rights, minimum tombstone and post-write checks validate
effects: current data changes without erasing accountable issuance and status history

owner_package_requirements: Dimension identity, owner, credential governance authority, issuer registry and privacy and records stewards
Credential-class, claim-schema, issuer-authority, status-method, trust, presentation-profile and retention registries
Master mappings for issuers, subjects, holders, verifiers, mandates, evidence, keys, grants, policies, decisions and audit logs
Issuance, validity, status, proof, disclosure, verification, correction, access, retention and agent-operation policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint stable IDs for credential classes and issued attestation instances. Preserve authoritative issuer serials and external subject, issuer, key, mandate and evidence identities; never use subject name, date or digest alone.
registry_links: Dimension-local credential-class, issuer, schema, status, trust and profile registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize an issued instance by authoritative issuer plus credential identifier under a versioned profile, not by subject name, serial alone, claim values, timestamp or proof digest.
Secure representation canonicalization, schema, vocabulary, proof, status and presentation versions are explicit and never inferred solely from file format.
patch_rules: Extensions declare credential family, target finding, claim semantics, issuer authority, validity, status, proof, privacy and interoperability impact.
Issued claims are immutable. Corrections, renewals, schema changes and representation upgrades create successor revisions or credentials with migration mappings and preserved provenance.
compatibility_rules: Unknown additive fields may be ignored only when identity, issuer, subject, claims, validity, proof, status, access and provenance remain intact.
Every VC, Data Integrity, X.509, SD-JWT or OpenID4VP mapping pins versions and states omissions, semantic conflicts, privacy changes and round-trip limits.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system credential or attestation identifier qualified by issuer and class.
Governed globally resolvable credential IRI or certificate issuer and serial tuple.
Dimension UUID when no authoritative or governed global identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; separate issuance, delivery, valid-from, valid-until, status, presentation, receipt, verification, decision and knowledge times.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {credential-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use subject name, issuer serial alone, date or digest alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, credential and representation binding, schema and proof versions, issuer and subject references, event and knowledge times, status freshness, access marking and provenance.

policies: Credential authenticity, integrity, current status, issuer authority, claim truth, subject control, authorization, eligibility and business acceptance are separate attributable judgments.
Holder custody does not make the holder the subject or issuer, and a licence or permit credential may evidence but does not replace the external permission-bearing grant.
Issued claims are immutable; correction, renewal, suspension, revocation and supersession append events and lineage and never silently rewrite issuer history.

Agents may perform allowlisted reversible validation and projection, but issuance, revocation, broader disclosure, trust-policy change and destructive disposition require delegated authority and policy-defined confirmation.

read: Resolve Dimension policy, credential profile, issuer authority, subject binding, current lineage head, proof and status methods, status freshness, trust inputs and access purpose.
create: Define class and schema before issuing; record issuer mandate, subject binding, claims, evidence, validity, status method, representation and provenance atomically.
update: Append delivery, status, presentation, verification, correction, renewal or supersession events with actor, authority, reason, event and knowledge time and provenance; never overwrite issued claims.
delete: Apply subject-rights, retention, legal-hold and audit policy; remove eligible holder copies, presentation data or expired proof material only through authorized disposition while preserving required issuer lineage and tombstone evidence.

access.default_rule: Deny claim values, issuance evidence, private subject identifiers, holder inventory, presentation history and correlation handles; publish only minimum status or credential data authorized for a purpose.
exceptions: Issuer, holder, subject-self, auditor, regulator, incident-response or court access cites authority and remains minimum-necessary, attributable, time-limited and separately logged.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, credential, operation, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected claims or status, source revision and outcome without copying protected claim content unnecessarily.

coverage.claim: Covers the issued attestation/credential aggregate from class and claim semantics through issuance, validity, status, securing, presentation, verification, loss-aware projection and governed disposition, grounded in eleven tier-1 W3C, IETF, OpenID Foundation and NIST sources whose citations are topically consistent with the findings that invoke them. This is explicitly not universal coverage: ISO/IEC 18013-5 mdoc, eIDAS/EUDI, sectoral credential families, legal-effect and accreditation regimes, and the VC JOSE/COSE securing path are absent or source-thin; question kinds and artifact identity are template-generated rather than analytically derived; no relation rows are approved; and no independent second-provider review exists under the owner waiver.

known_omissions: No independent Claude or Grok result was available; later credential, PKI, privacy and legal review is required before canonical promotion.
No approved relation rows were supplied; proposed links to identity, mandate, evidence, key, grant, policy, decision and audit models remain holds.
National identity documents, mobile driving licences, professional licences, academic credentials, health certificates and regulated trust services require separate profiles.
X.509 and OCSP have later updates and deployment profiles; certified processing and algorithm suites require profile-specific review.
conflicts: An authentic credential may contain a disputed or stale claim, come from an untrusted issuer or be irrelevant to a relying-party decision.
Holder, subject and presenter can be different parties and holder binding can increase privacy risk or correlation.
Revocation freshness, offline verification, availability, privacy and status-list correlation impose competing requirements.
regional_assumptions: Legal effect, issuer qualification, subject rights, retention, revocation reasons and recognition depend on jurisdiction and sector.
W3C and OpenID specifications define technical data and protocol models but do not establish universal issuer trust or authorization.
NIST guidance focuses on digital identity services and does not define every civil, professional, product or organizational credential.
adversarial_checks: Reject an issued credential whose class, issuer authority, subject binding, claims, validity, schema or current lineage cannot be resolved.
Reject technical proof success represented as claim truth, issuer trust, authorization, eligibility or legal effect.
Reject silent claim mutation, status removal, identifier reuse, renewal without lineage or correction without issuer authority.
Reject a presentation that is unbound to request, audience, nonce or purpose where the profile requires them, or that discloses more than authorized.
Reject an agent operation that issues, revokes, broadens disclosure, changes trust or destroys held evidence without delegated authority.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two axes must be separated. On the record plane, a frozen registry value such as standalone-mm classifies how the entry is stored and governed in the registry, not what the subject is; it is never a subject-model entry kind. The pack ships frozen_context as an empty object, so the registry value could not be re-read here and its cross-check is held. On the subject-model plane, the declared 'mixin' is not defensible against the provider's own evidence: the model mints and canonicalizes issued-instance identity (authoritative issuer plus credential identifier), owns an append-only lifecycle with activate/suspend/revoke/renew/correct/supersede events, defines disposition authority, legal hold, tombstones, an artifact identity priority ladder and seven steward roles. A mixin is a reusable trait attached to a host entity and owns no independent identity, retention authority or delete policy. 'aggregate' is preferred over 'entity' because credential class, typed claims, secured representations, proofs, status entries, presentations, disclosure manifests and receipts are non-independent parts governed under a single root, and the provider's own coverage claim already calls the subject 'an issued attestation and credential aggregate'. Status is reclassified rather than split, but presentation and disclosure ownership is recorded as the leading split candidate because a presentation binds a set of credentials from possibly several issuers and cannot canonicalize under one credential identifier.

decisions.rationale: The scope statement, canonicalization rules, artifact identity ladder, CRUD delete policy and steward roles all describe a root that owns instance identity and retention authority; a mixin owns none of these, and the provider's own coverage claim already names the subject an aggregate.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root = issued credential instance qualified by issuing authority
decisions.rationale: Canonicalization by authoritative issuer plus credential identifier, with explicit refusal of subject name, issuer serial alone, timestamp, claim values or proof digest as identity, is internally consistent across canon_and_patch, artifact_rules and every artifact identity_strategy, and matches SRC-001 and SRC-005 identity practice.

decisions.concept: Presentation, disclosure manifest and receipt ownership inside the credential aggregate
decisions.rationale: A presentation carries its own identifier, holder binding, proof and a credential set that may span issuers, so it cannot canonicalize under the mandated {credential-id} serial rule; the boundary is retained for the draft but flagged for a split decision once relation rows exist.

decisions.concept: Verifier-authored presentation request as an owned function
decisions.rationale: create-presentation-request records verifier, purpose, audience, nonce and expiry, which are authored outside the credential aggregate; retaining it risks duplicating a Verifier or Request model, so it is kept as a reference-only record pending cross-model adjudication.

decisions.concept: Externalization of issuer, subject, holder, key, mandate, grant, decision and audit masters
decisions.rationale: out_of_scope, the five boundary_notes, the composition checklist row and the stated policies agree without contradiction, and this externalization is what keeps credential authenticity from collapsing into authorization, which is the central risk for this subject.

decisions.concept: Separation of technical verification from claim truth, issuer trust and authorization
decisions.rationale: This distinction is carried consistently by a dedicated finding with an explicit non-authorization marker, a service-layer policy, an adversarial check and a declared conflict, and is directly supported by SRC-001 and SRC-009; it is the strongest and most defensible part of the result.

decisions.concept: Three-question template with rotated kind labels
decisions.rationale: All 24 findings carry the same three question stems and the kind values rotate mechanically, so an identity-shaped stem is labelled 'ownership' and the histogram is a flat 3 per kind with validation at 6; the labels are generation artifacts and must not be published as evidence of analytic coverage.

decisions.concept: Uniform artifact media_or_form and slug-derived identity_strategy
decisions.rationale: All 24 artifacts share identical media_or_form and a strategy templated from the finding slug, which omits the artifact-kind token that serial_naming_rule mandates and couples durable artifact identity to editorial slugs; the naming rule and the strategies must be reconciled before freeze.

decisions.concept: Identifier and name drift across findings
decisions.rationale: disclosure-consent-authority-... is named 'Disclosure authority, ...' with consent dropped, and the licence/license spelling differs between id and name; because ids are load-bearing for artifact identity, drift must be reconciled rather than silently tolerated.

decisions.concept: Coverage checklist marking all sixteen dimensions covered
decisions.disposition: rejected - downgrade spatial and interoperability to partial
decisions.rationale: The spatial note concedes jurisdiction is referenced only when material, and interoperability claims loss-aware projections while omitting ISO/IEC 18013-5 mdoc and the VC JOSE/COSE securing path; a fully covered checklist also contradicts the declared medium confidence and the known omissions list.

decisions.concept: Legal effect, accreditation and recognition finding source support
decisions.rationale: The finding cites only SRC-001, SRC-005 and SRC-009, none of which establish legal effect, issuer accreditation or mutual recognition, so no legal-effect assertion may be published until a legal or conformity-assessment authority is added.

decisions.concept: Source version pins including RFC 9901 and four co-dated W3C Recommendations
decisions.rationale: A no-tools audit cannot confirm that SD-JWT is RFC 9901 dated November 2025, that SRC-001 to SRC-004 all carry the 15 May 2025 Recommendation date, or that RFC 6960 is updated by RFC 8954 and RFC 9654; each pin must be re-resolved against the live source before promotion.

audit_requirements permits logging affected claims qualified only by 'unnecessarily', which is too weak beside a deny-by-default rule on claim values; the log must be constrained to claim paths, status references and outcomes rather than claim content.

decisions.concept: Immutable issued claims versus subject erasure and disposition rights
decisions.rationale: The delete rules assert both issuer-lineage immutability and subject-rights disposition without a precedence test or a tombstone specification, so retention guidance cannot be published as normative until the jurisdictional precedence rule is settled.

decisions.concept: Absence of a subject-initiated contest or dispute intake function
decisions.rationale: Every third question asks how the item is contested, yet the ten functions expose only issuer-side correction; the missing intake path is recorded for a later provider pass rather than added here, because add_functions must remain empty under the single-provider waiver.

All links to identity, mandate, evidence, key, grant, policy, decision and audit models remain unapproved proposals in known_omissions, so the deterministic synthesizer must emit no relationship edges for this record.

publicationHolds: Live source and version verification is outstanding for all eleven sources; RFC 9901 as Selective Disclosure for JSON Web Tokens dated November 2025, the four W3C Recommendations all dated 15 May 2025, the OpenID4VP final of 9 July 2025, NIST SP 800-63-4 of July 2025 and the RFC 6960 update chain must each be re-resolved before canonical promotion.

Independent second-provider review is absent by explicit repository-owner waiver of both Claude and Grok; this Codex result plus a local no-tools adversarial audit is not external review and must be shown as such in every publication artifact.

The record must publish as reviewable-draft with the corrected subject-model entry kind aggregate, and must state that the frozen registry classification is a record-plane value that was not re-readable here because frozen_context was empty.
No approved relation rows exist; all proposed links to identity, mandate, evidence, key, grant, policy, decision and audit models stay unpublished holds and no relationship edges may be emitted.

Question kind labels are template rotations and artifact media_or_form and identity strategies are boilerplate; both must be re-derived, and identity strategies reconciled with the {credential-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id} rule, before any freeze.
The jurisdiction, accreditation, legal effect and recognition finding is held from publication as a normative statement until a legal or conformity-assessment authority supports it.

Presentation, disclosure manifest and receipt ownership is held as an unresolved split candidate because presentation identity spans multiple credentials and cannot canonicalize under a single credential identifier.

The coverage checklist may not publish as sixteen-of-sixteen covered; spatial and interoperability must be downgraded to partial and the no-universal-completeness statement carried alongside the coverage claim.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Resolve whether ISO/IEC 18013-5 mdoc and the eIDAS 2.0 / EUDI Wallet architecture belong in the crosswalk finding or in an explicit out-of-scope statement, given that OpenID4VP is widely deployed with mdoc and the model already claims loss-aware projections.

Add or explicitly exclude the W3C Securing Verifiable Credentials using JOSE and COSE specification; the secured-representation finding talks about envelopes and detached content while citing only the Data Integrity path.
Confirm the SD-JWT publication identity and number, and determine whether SD-JWT VC is a distinct source needed for credential-type binding beyond the base selective-disclosure mechanism.

Establish a legal and conformity-assessment source set for issuer accreditation, legal effect and mutual recognition so the recognition-profile finding is not carried on identity and PKI sources alone.
Settle the precedence rule between immutable issuer lineage and subject erasure or disposition rights, including a tombstone specification, before retention guidance is published as normative.

Design the subject-initiated contest and dispute intake path that the question set assumes but the ten functions do not expose, and decide whether it is an owned function or an external decision model reference.

Compare status-list herd privacy against OCSP request privacy and offline verification to produce a defensible freshness and correlation policy rather than the current statement of competing requirements.

Test the holder-copy custody boundary against the declared external wallet inventory, since the model owns delivery, custody, presentation history and disposition of holder representations while disclaiming wallet inventory.

model.name: Subscription
model.purpose: Represent one governed recurring commercial relationship so agents can understand who subscribes to which plan, which items and entitlements recur, how billing and renewal operate, what usage and service evidence exists and how cancellation progresses without confusing the subscription with its contract, invoices, payments or service instances.
model.scope_statement: Owns subscription identity, versions, profile and lifecycle; provider, subscriber, payer, beneficiary and administrator references; external contract, account, order, catalogue, offering, service and entitlement bindings; plan versions, items, add-ons, bundles, seats, assignments and dependencies; permissions, limits, usage allowances, rollover and overage references; recurring, one-time, seat, usage and tiered price rules; currencies, taxes, discounts, credits, proration and refunds; billing anchors, recurrence, periods, invoice and payment references; trial, activation, service, pause, suspension, grace and reactivation observations; term, renewal, notice, consent, cancellation and termination assertions; usage, quality, support, provenance, validation, privacy, retention and loss-aware projections. External agreement, party, product, entitlement, order, invoice, payment, usage, service, support and records masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Subscription identity, versions, profiles, participants, plan bindings, items, seats, beneficiaries, entitlements, usage allowances and constraints
Recurring economics, billing and renewal schedules, invoice and payment references, service and usage evidence, lifecycle, notices, cancellation, validation, access, retention and projections
out_of_scope: Owning Contract, Party, Account, Product, Service Offering, Entitlement, Credential, Order, Invoice, Payment Method, Payment Transaction, Usage Event, Meter Reading, Service Instance, Support Case or Records masters
Treating active, paid, renewed or cancelled status as universal proof of legal validity, service delivery, entitlement, conformity, termination completion or data deletion
Autonomous contract formation, charging, invoicing, plan or price change, entitlement grant or revocation, renewal, cancellation, termination, disclosure or physical records disposition

boundary_notes.distinction: The unfrozen parent agreement establishes obligations and legal terms. The subscription is a recurring operational aggregate that references but does not replace the contract.
The plan or offering defines reusable terms, products and services have independent instances, and entitlements are separate grants. The subscription binds versions and observes state.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Invoice, payment mandate, payment and usage
boundary_notes.distinction: Billing schedules predict or request recurring economics, invoices assert amounts due, payments settle, and usage observations meter consumption; none is the subscription identity.
Activation, entitlement, provisioning and availability are separate processes or observations; active subscription status does not prove their success.

boundary_notes.neighbor: TM Forum, schema.org, ODRL, EPC, RFC, PROV, DQV and OpenAPI
boundary_notes.distinction: Each representation has a distinct scope; every mapping is version-pinned and loss-declaring.

boundaryDecision.rationale: The root is a recurring commercial-relationship aggregate. Contract, party, account, plan or offering, product, service, entitlement, order, invoice, payment, usage event, meter reading, service instance, support case and records remain external masters.

decisions.concept: Subscription, contract, plan, membership and entitlement
decisions.rationale: The subscription binds an agreement and versioned plan to recurring operational and economic context; it is neither the reusable plan nor the legal contract, membership identity or entitlement grant.
Commercial Contract is a plausible parent reference, but no frozen canonical relation grants ownership, mutation or cascade authority.
Provider, subscriber, customer, payer, beneficiary, seat holder, administrator, agent and sponsor remain separate, source-qualified roles and may be different parties.

decisions.concept: Agreement, entitlement, provisioning, service, billing, payment and usage axes
decisions.rationale: Each axis preserves independent state, authority, evidence and time; active, paid or renewed status cannot prove the others.
Recurring, one-time, seat, usage, tiered, volume, tax, discount, credit, proration, refund and overage values remain distinct and source-qualified.
Anchor, timezone, interval, in-advance or arrears basis, exceptions, count or end, invoice and due times stay explicit; a schedule neither invoices nor charges.
Request, notice, at-period-end selection, immediate effect, termination completion, entitlement revocation, final bill, refund, export and deletion remain separately attributable.
EU consumer and digital-content rules, UNIDROIT Principles and EPC direct-debit rules are scoped profiles rather than universal subscription law.
TM Forum, schema.org, ODRL, EPC, RFC, PROV, DQV, ISO 4217 and OpenAPI cover different facets and never replace the canonical aggregate.

One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audits the frozen validated result and comparison locally without tools or new research facts; assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-ECO-022 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external research result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-ECO-006 is only a parent signal and no model relation is canonically approved for this aggregate.

Boundary hold: subscription, contract, party, account, plan, offering, product, service, entitlement, order, invoice, payment, usage event, meter reading, support case and records must retain separate identities.
State-axis hold: agreement, entitlement, provisioning, availability, billing, payment, usage, support and cancellation states and clocks must never be silently collapsed.

Economic hold: every recurring, one-time, seat, usage, tiered, tax, discount, credit, proration, refund and overage value requires currency, quantity or usage basis, period, source, approval and uncertainty.

Temporal hold: signup, contract, trial, activation, service, usage, billing, invoice, payment, renewal, notice, cancellation, termination, observation, ingestion and knowledge time remain distinct; timestamps require seconds and timezone offset.
Cancellation hold: request, notice, effective cancellation, termination completion, entitlement revocation, final billing, refund, export and data disposition require separate evidence and authority.

Authority hold: contract formation, plan or price change, charging, invoicing, entitlement grant or revocation, renewal, cancellation, termination, disclosure and disposition require delegated accountable authority.
Jurisdiction hold: EU consumer and digital-content rules, UNIDROIT Principles and EPC direct-debit rules are scoped profiles; national and sector rules require separate validation.

Interoperability hold: every TM Forum, schema.org, ODRL, EPC, RFC 5545, RFC 3339, PROV, DQV, ISO 4217 and OpenAPI projection requires version pins, conformance evidence and information-loss declarations.
Privacy hold: personal, usage, device, location, entitlement, payment, delinquency, support and cancellation data require purpose-bound access, minimization, portability and retention controls.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.

owner_package_requirements: Declare award-record owner and authorized steward.

dimension.namespace_guidance: Use issuer-qualified award IDs; keep subject, scheme, envelope and local revision IDs distinct. Do not expose private identity in public paths.
registry_links: Status observation and protected evidence registry

canonicalization_rules: Preserve source vocabulary, award scope and authority qualifiers.
Separate effective intervals, envelope periods and observation times; unknown is not active.
patch_rules: Pin base version and digest; namespace profession and jurisdiction profiles.
Append corrections under expected-head checks; retain competing reports where permitted.
compatibility_rules: Do not merge license, certification, membership and qualification semantics.
Refuse export when required scope, status freshness or authority qualifiers would be lost.

artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 seconds and explicit offset or Z for recording instants; preserve date-only and uncertain effective periods separately.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Opaque award ID, record kind and revision; no personal names or disciplinary details in filenames.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Check exact-byte digest and revision; integrity never proves issuer authority or permission to practise.

policies: No real issuance, revocation, regulator contact or personal-record lookup follows from filling this model.
Never equate good signature, active local record, qualification and current practice permission.
Treat unavailable or stale status as unknown under the relying policy, not good standing.
Collect only necessary authorized evidence and protect disciplinary or assessment details.

read: Read Dimension policy, pinned specification, assurance holds and permitted evidence scope before accessing award records.
create: Record an authorized attributed award assertion; keep unknown issuer/subject binding explicit.
update: Append status observations or corrections with evidence, effective time and expected-head guard; local edit cannot reverse issuer decisions.
delete: Apply retention, legal holds and justified deletion to local records; preserve only permitted minimal tombstones. Local deletion does not revoke an award.

model.name: Legal Instrument / Norm
model.purpose: Represent an authority-backed legal instrument and the norms expressed by its addressable source fragments, independent of storage and interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns legal-work, expression, manifestation, source, provision and norm linkage; instrument class; authority and legal-basis references; structure and citations; authenticity and provenance; deontic assertions; lifecycle, temporal applicability, interpretation, access and projections. Organizations, lawmaking procedures, cases, enforcement events, affected parties, places and generic document storage remain external masters.
in_scope: Legal work, expression, manifestation, item, authoritative source, provision and norm identity
Authority, class, structure, citation, normative meaning, lifecycle, time, applicability, conflict and provenance
Authentication, consolidation, controlled disclosure, retention, interoperability and safe agent operations
out_of_scope: Issuing organization, legislative or administrative procedure and generic document repository masters
Court or arbitration case, enforcement event, affected person, asset and place masters
Automated legal advice, universally binding interpretation or substantive law common to every jurisdiction

boundary_notes.distinction: Authorities are external organizations referenced in a specific legal capacity; the legal instrument owns neither their identity nor governance.
The process produces adoption and publication evidence; the instrument aggregate preserves outputs and lifecycle assertions but not the workflow master.
A case may interpret, invalidate or apply an instrument, but its parties, procedure, evidence and decision lifecycle remain a separate model.
A policy or rule may lack legal-source authority; this aggregate requires explicit legal-source, jurisdiction and competent-authority bindings.
Files and records are manifestations or evidence items; they do not replace authority-qualified legal-work identity or normative semantics.

preconditions: publisher role and evidence are known
effects: official and unofficial copies remain distinguishable

functions.name: Address provision and citation

preconditions: source versions and numbering history resolve
effects: provisions stay citable across rendition and renumbering

functions.name: Bind norm to source

preconditions: source fragments and expression version resolve
effects: formal semantics remain attributable and contestable

functions.name: Record legal lifecycle event

preconditions: competence, affected scope and times validate
effects: state changes without overwriting prior assertions

model.name: Assessment / Evaluation
model.purpose: Give an agent the context needed to understand, create, inspect and operate an assessment or evaluation record: what was assessed, against which criteria at which version, by which method, on what evidence, yielding which criterion outcomes, scores, composite result and stated conclusion, with declared validity, assurance, lifecycle, disclosure and interoperability.
model.scope_statement: Format-neutral structure of a single assessment/evaluation instance and the bindings it carries to reusable definitional components (criteria source, instrument, scale, decision rule). It spans framing and scoping, criteria binding and tailoring, method and execution parameters, evidence and observation capture, criterion-level determination, aggregation, conclusion and validity, assurance of assessor competence and impartiality, and record lifecycle, disclosure, retention referral and external projection. It is subject-domain agnostic and applies equally to conformity assessment, security control assessment, accessibility evaluation, educational measurement, clinical risk assessment and peer review. It is modelled as an aggregate because the assessment act, its inputs and its determinations share one identity boundary and one finalisation event.
in_scope: Identity, granularity and versioning of an assessment record and its supersession chain
Assessment type, stakes, mandate, scheme reference and first/second/third-party relationship
Subject reference, pinned assessed state, scope boundary, sampling and generalisation limits
Binding of criteria to a named catalogue at a pinned version, plus selection, tailoring and interpretation notes
Declared method, mode, depth and coverage, and the instrument or rubric that operationalises each criterion
Execution parameters needed for reproducibility: tool and model references, versions, configuration, input snapshots
Evidence item references, criterion linkage, sufficiency, admissibility and confidentiality qualifiers
Observation records with distinct event and recording times, plus declared uncertainty and traceability pointers
Criterion-level outcomes, rationale, severity and locators; raw, normalised and maximum scores
Aggregation model, weighting, composite score or level, and result-vector expression
Conclusion statement, decision authority, qualifications, dissent, validity window and surveillance obligations
Assessor identity and roles, competence and authorisation references, impartiality and conflict declarations
Independent review, moderation, rater agreement, and validity/reliability/fairness evidence for the instrument
Record state machine, correction, appeal and supersession; disclosure classification, redaction and retention referral
Crosswalks and vocabulary bindings for projection into external assessment reporting formats
out_of_scope: Internal structure, lifecycle and state management of the assessed subject itself
Authoring, versioning, publication and normative interpretation of the criteria catalogue or standard
Runtime execution and orchestration of testing tools, scanners, graders or evaluator engines and their operational telemetry
Issuance, signing, suspension, withdrawal and verification of certificates, credentials or attestations
Enforcement of consequences: certification decisions with legal effect, licensing, sanction, market withdrawal or remediation workflow
Identity management, employment and qualification records of persons and organisations
Physical or digital custody, storage and chain-of-custody execution for evidence objects
Calibration programmes, metrological traceability management and instrument maintenance
Training, validation and deployment lifecycle of predictive or generative scoring engines
Platform audit-trail and access-log semantics, storage and evaluation
Execution of retention, destruction, transfer or erasure actions
Risk register lifecycle, risk treatment and plan-of-action-and-milestones case management
Population-level aggregation of many assessments into reputation scores or league tables
Commercial terms, scheduling and cost accounting of assessment services

boundary_notes.distinction: An assessment consumes measured or observed values as evidence and adds criterion-referenced judgement; a bare measured value with an uncertainty statement is a measurement result, not an assessment. Units, uncertainty evaluation and calibration traceability are referenced from the metrology model.

This model carries a criterion reference, its pinned catalogue version, local applicability and interpretation notes only. Criterion text, structure, normative status and catalogue lifecycle belong to the catalogue, exactly as OSCAL separates a control catalogue from assessment results and XCCDF separates a Benchmark from a TestResult.

ISO/IEC 17000 separates determination and review from decision and from attestation. This model ends at the recorded conclusion; issuing, signing, suspending or revoking a certificate or credential is a downstream act, and in EU product law only a designated notified body may give that act legal effect.

EARL records the assertor and the test mode as attributes of an assertion, and XCCDF records the checking system as a reference. Naming a tool, its version and its configuration never transfers ownership of running that tool, its scheduling, or its operational logs.

OSCAL keeps observations, findings and risks distinct and hands risks onward to a POA&M. This model may produce findings that seed risks, but risk characterisation lifecycle, mitigating factors, remediation tracking and deadlines belong to the risk model.

Assessor identity, competence evidence, accreditation and designation scope are referenced by identifier and version. Whether a body is accredited or notified, and for what scope, is asserted and maintained by the accreditation authority, not by an assessment record.

Content provenance (which agent produced which determination, from which evidence, when) is mixed in from a PROV-aligned model and retained. Platform-level record access and change logging is a separate audit model whose storage and evaluation this model does not own.

This model declares a retention class, a retention trigger event and a legal-hold flag, and records the referral. Setting periods and executing destruction, transfer or erasure is owned by the adopting Dimension's records policy.

schema.org AggregateRating rolls many individual ratings into counts and averages across a population. That population-level statistic is a sibling concern; this model bounds one assessment occasion on one declared subject and scope.

A conformity assessment scheme, examination programme or continuous-monitoring programme defines recurring rules, cycles and eligibility. This model references the scheme and carries the parameters it fixed for this occasion; the scheme's own rules and cycle belong to the programme model.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 17000:2020 Conformity assessment — Vocabulary and general principles
sources.relevance: Canonical vocabulary for the functional approach to conformity assessment — object of conformity assessment, specified requirement, selection, determination, review, decision, attestation and surveillance — which grounds the separation of determination from decision and from attestation in this model. Catalogue record and the review/decision/attestation definitions were verified; the full text is paywalled and was not retrieved.

sources.title: OSCAL Assessment Results Model (Assessment Layer)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Machine-readable assessment-results structure: reviewed-controls, assessment-subject, assessment-assets, attestation, assessment-log, and the explicit separation of observations (evidence) from findings (criterion-referenced determinations) from risks. Grounds evidence/observation/finding layering and the requirement to update record identity on change.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53A Rev. 5 — Assessing Security and Privacy Controls in Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Assessment procedures with determination statements, assessment methods (examine, interview, test), assessment objects (specifications, mechanisms, activities, individuals), depth and coverage attributes, and satisfied / other-than-satisfied findings. Grounds the method, depth/coverage and criterion-verdict findings.

sources.title: NISTIR 7275 Rev. 4 — Specification for the Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) Version 1.2
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Benchmark/Rule/Group/Value/Profile definitions versus TestResult and rule-result instances; scoring models (default, flat, flat-unweighted, absolute); and a nine-value result vocabulary including notapplicable, notchecked, notselected, error and informational. Grounds scale, aggregation and indeterminate-outcome handling.

sources.title: Evaluation and Report Language (EARL) 1.0 Schema
sources.relevance: Minimal normative shape of an evaluation assertion: assertedBy, subject, test, result and mode, with OutcomeValue (passed, failed, cantTell, inapplicable, untested) and TestMode (automatic, manual, semiAuto, undisclosed). Grounds the assertion quadruple, indeterminate outcomes and mode declaration.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent with wasGeneratedBy, used, wasAssociatedWith, wasAttributedTo, wasDerivedFrom, actedOnBehalfOf, startedAtTime/endedAtTime, Plan and Role. Grounds the provenance mix-in, attribution of determinations to assessors and the derivation chain from evidence to conclusion.

sources.title: FHIR R5 RiskAssessment resource
sources.relevance: A domain assessment record with identifier, status, method, code, subject, occurrence, performer, basis (source data), prediction with probability/qualitativeRisk/when/rationale, and mitigation. Grounds subject/method/basis/prediction separation, status vocabulary and the assessment-versus-observation boundary.

sources.title: Question and Test Interoperability (QTI) 3.0 — Implementation and Best Practices
sources.relevance: Item and test structure with responseDeclaration, outcomeDeclaration, responseProcessing, SCORE/MAXSCORE outcomes, sessionStatus, and a separate results-reporting model (assessmentResult, itemResult, testResult). Grounds instrument/item definition, raw-versus-maximum score and separation of instrument definition from result records.

sources.title: Common Vulnerability Scoring System v4.0 Specification Document
sources.organization: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST)
sources.relevance: A governed scoring specification with metric groups, a mandatory vector string published alongside the numeric score, and a qualitative severity band mapping. Grounds the rule that a published score must travel with the inputs, scale and model that produced it.

sources.title: Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation, CC:2022 Release 1, and CEM:2022
sources.version_or_date: CC:2022 Release 1 with Errata v1.2; CC v3.1 R5 usable to 30 June 2024
sources.relevance: Five-part evaluation framework (general model, functional components, assurance components, framework for evaluation methods and activities, predefined packages) plus a separate evaluation methodology. Grounds the separation of criteria catalogue, evaluation method specification and evaluation instance, and the notion of predefined assurance packages.

sources.title: ILAC-G8:09/2019 Guidelines on Decision Rules and Statements of Conformity (ILAC Guidance Series)
sources.relevance: Decision rules for issuing statements of conformity to a specification, as required of laboratories by ISO/IEC 17025:2017, covering how uncertainty is handled before a pass/fail statement. Grounds the decision-rule, threshold and abstention finding and the report-identity strategy.

sources.title: Conformity assessment (Single Market — Goods, building blocks)
sources.relevance: Regulated conformity assessment: manufacturer-performed versus notified-body assessment, the declaration of conformity content, CE marking sequencing, and the explicit warning that certificates from non-notified bodies have no legal value. Grounds the mandate/authority findings and the rule that legal effect is not inferable from method quality.

sources.title: Website Accessibility Conformance Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM) 2.0
sources.relevance: Five-step evaluation methodology: define scope, explore the target, select a representative sample (structured plus ~10% random), evaluate, and report; plus the explicit limit that conformance claims cannot be made for a whole product from a sampled subset. Grounds scope/sampling/generalisation and optional aggregated scoring with documented methodology.

sources.title: schema.org Rating, Review and AggregateRating types
sources.relevance: Widely deployed minimal rating vocabulary: ratingValue with bestRating/worstRating bounds, ratingExplanation, reviewAspect, author and itemReviewed, plus AggregateRating counts. Grounds scale-bound and direction declaration and marks the boundary to population-level aggregation.

sources.title: JCGM publications, including JCGM 106:2012 The role of measurement uncertainty in conformity assessment and JCGM 100:2008 (GUM)
sources.organization: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology (BIPM)
sources.relevance: Authoritative treatment of measurement uncertainty and its role in conformity decisions, and the metrological vocabulary for quantity, unit, measurement result and traceability. Grounds the uncertainty/traceability finding and the requirement to state uncertainty before deciding conformity.

sources.title: Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing (open-access edition)
sources.relevance: Joint professional standards treating validity, reliability/precision and fairness as foundations, with operations chapters on test design, scores and cut scores, administration, scoring, reporting, supporting documentation and test-taker rights. Grounds the validity/reliability/fairness evidence finding and appeal rights of the assessed subject.

bundles.name: Assessment Frame, Subject and Scope
bundles.description: What this assessment is, who mandated it, what it is about, and where its boundary lies.
bundles.rationale: Every reviewed standard begins by fixing an object of assessment and a bounded scope before any criterion is applied: OSCAL names an assessment-subject and reviewed-controls, WCAG-EM makes scope definition and sampling the first two steps, and FHIR RiskAssessment requires a subject. Framing errors invalidate everything downstream, so identity, mandate, subject and scope are grouped as one top-level concern.

data_elements.name: Assessment identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the assessment record, with its issuing scheme.

data_elements.name: Assessment version
data_elements.description: Version label or sequence of this revision of the assessment.

data_elements.name: Supersedes reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the assessment version this record replaces.

data_elements.name: Record granularity
data_elements.description: Declared unit of record (subject-occasion, subject-criteria-set, campaign item).

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity, granularity and supersession are pure reference data carried on the record itself — identifier values, scheme names and pointers. Nothing is rendered, captured or attached here; any document that displays these values is produced by the conclusion or disclosure findings, so declaring an artifact would duplicate them.

findings.name: Assessment type, stakes and mandate
findings.description: The class of assessment, the party relationship between assessor and subject, the scheme or legal basis authorising it, and the consequence class its result carries.

questions.text: Which class of assessment is this: conformity, diagnostic, formative, summative, risk, quality, appraisal or peer review?
answer_data: Assessment type code and its code system

questions.text: Is this a first-party, second-party or third-party assessment relative to the subject?
Under what mandate, scheme or legal basis is the assessment carried out?
answer_data: Scheme or programme reference with version
Legal, regulatory or contractual basis citation
Designation or notification reference where legal effect is claimed

questions.text: What consequences attach to the result, and who commissioned it?

data_elements.name: Assessment type
data_elements.description: Coded class of assessment.

data_elements.name: Party relationship
data_elements.description: First-, second- or third-party relationship of assessor to subject.

data_elements.name: Scheme reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the conformity assessment scheme, programme or examination framework.

data_elements.name: Consequence class
data_elements.description: Declared class of consequence attaching to the result.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are classificatory and authority-bearing reference values that qualify the record. The scheme document, the legal instrument and the party records they point to are held and versioned by referenced sibling models, so materialising a local artifact would copy content this model must not own.

layers.name: Subject and Scope
layers.description: What was assessed, in what state, and how the assessed boundary and sample were drawn.

findings.name: Subject identification and assessed state
findings.description: Which object of assessment was examined, at which pinned version, configuration or state, whether it is an individual, batch, population or system, and where it was located when that matters.

questions.text: Which identifier and identifier scheme designate the object of assessment?
answer_data: Subject reference with its owning model

questions.text: What version, configuration or state of the subject was assessed, and how is that state pinned?
answer_data: Pinned state descriptor (version, build, configuration hash)
Method used to pin the state
Time at which the state was fixed

questions.text: Is the subject an individual item, a batch, a population or a system, and how is membership defined?
Where was the subject located or deployed at the time of assessment, when location affects the result?

data_elements.name: Subject reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the assessed object in its owning domain model.

data_elements.name: Subject kind
data_elements.description: Whether the subject is an item, batch, population, system, person or process.

data_elements.name: Assessed state descriptor
data_elements.description: Pinned version, build or configuration identifier of the subject as assessed.

data_elements.name: Subject site reference
data_elements.description: Location or deployment context of the subject during assessment.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The subject's own description, structure and lifecycle belong to its domain model; this finding holds only a reference plus a pinned state descriptor. Attaching a subject artifact here would reproduce target-owned content and create a second, divergent copy of the subject record.

findings.name: Scope boundary, sampling and generalisation limits
findings.description: What was explicitly inside and outside the assessed scope, how a sample was selected and sized if the whole subject was not assessed, and how far the result may legitimately be generalised.

questions.text: What is explicitly inside and outside the assessed scope?
answer_data: Boundary conditions and interfaces treated as external

questions.text: If a sample was assessed rather than the whole subject, how was the sample selected and sized?
To what extent may the result be generalised beyond the assessed sample or scope?
What happens to the assessment if the scope changes while it is in progress?

data_elements.name: Scope statement
data_elements.description: Declared inclusions and exclusions of the assessment.

data_elements.name: Sampling strategy
data_elements.description: Coded strategy used to select the assessed sample.

data_elements.name: Sample size
data_elements.description: Number of items assessed and the population size where known.

data_elements.name: Generalisation limit
data_elements.description: Statement of how far the result may be extended beyond the sample.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Scope, sampling design and generalisation limits are declarative statements and counts that must be readable inline by any consumer before it trusts a conclusion. WCAG-EM treats them as reported steps rather than deliverables, and the sampled items themselves are registered as evidence references elsewhere.

bundles.name: Criteria, Method and Scale
bundles.description: Which criteria apply at which version, how they were examined, and the scale and decision rule by which results are expressed and decided.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL, XCCDF and Common Criteria all keep a versioned criteria catalogue separate from the instance that binds it, and all reviewed formats require an explicit method and result vocabulary. ILAC-G8 and JCGM 106 additionally require an explicit decision rule before a conformity statement. Binding, method and decision rule together determine whether a result is interpretable and reproducible.

layers.name: Criteria Binding
layers.description: Reference and version binding to the criteria source, and which criteria were selected, excluded or added.

findings.name: Criterion reference and version binding
findings.description: The catalogue, standard or rubric supplying the criteria, the version pinned for this assessment, the locator for each individual criterion, and any interpretation applied to ambiguous criterion text.

questions.text: Which criteria catalogue, standard or rubric supplies the criteria, at which version?
answer_data: Criteria source reference and owning model
Publisher and authority of the source

questions.text: How is an individual criterion addressed unambiguously within that source?
answer_data: Path or clause locator within the source

questions.text: Where the criterion text is ambiguous, which interpretation or application note was applied?
answer_data: Reference to a published interpretation or technical decision

questions.text: How is the exact criteria version preserved so the result stays reproducible after the catalogue changes?
answer_data: Retained snapshot or digest of the bound criteria
Policy on recomputation when the catalogue changes

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding deliberately carries only a reference, a pinned version and a locator. The criterion's normative text, structure and lifecycle are owned by the criteria catalogue model; embedding them as an artifact here would duplicate target-owned content and let a local copy drift from the authoritative source.

findings.name: Criterion selection, applicability and tailoring
findings.description: Which criteria from the bound source were selected, which were declared not applicable and why, and whether any criteria were added beyond the source and under whose authority.

Whether the addition affects claimed conformance to the source

findings.inline_only_rationale: Selection and tailoring are decisions about the referenced catalogue, expressible as identifier lists with justifications. Where a scheme publishes a reusable profile, that profile is a catalogue-side artifact referenced by identifier and version, not a document this model produces.

layers.name: Method and Execution
layers.description: How each criterion was examined and what must be preserved for the result to be reproducible.

Item or check identifiers bound to each criterion
Administration conditions required by the instrument

artifacts.name: Assessment procedure or plan
artifacts.description: The written or machine-readable procedure that states, per criterion, which methods, objects, depth and coverage apply for this assessment.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the procedure's own master-system identifier and version issued by its publisher; the assessment references it by identifier plus version, never by title. Where the procedure is written specifically for this assessment, it takes a Dimension-assigned UUID bound to the assessment identifier.

artifacts.name: Instrument, rubric or item-set definition
artifacts.description: The definition of the measuring instrument used: rubric levels, item bank, questionnaire or benchmark profile, including administration conditions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Publisher identifier plus edition or version for published instruments; a Dimension-assigned UUID plus version for locally authored instruments. Never identified by administration date.

findings.name: Execution parameters and reproducibility
findings.description: The tool, model or engine references, versions, configuration profiles and input snapshots that were in force when machine-generated results were produced, captured so an independent party can reproduce them.

What configuration, profile, thresholds and input data snapshot were in force during execution?
answer_data: Configuration or profile reference with version
Input dataset or snapshot reference with digest

questions.text: What must be preserved for an independent party to reproduce the same results?
answer_data: Retention requirement for the reproducibility bundle

data_elements.name: Tool or engine reference

artifacts.name: Execution parameter manifest
artifacts.description: An immutable capture of the tool references, versions, configuration and input snapshot digests that the assessment relies on. It documents parameters; it does not schedule, invoke or control any evaluator, which remains owned by the referenced execution model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Series key is the assessment identifier; a zero-padded monotonically increasing run sequence distinguishes manifests, with a cryptographic digest recorded at registration. The sequence is never derived from a date.

layers.name: Scale and Decision Rule
layers.description: The vocabulary and scale in which results are expressed, and the rule that converts them into a decision.

findings.name: Outcome scale and result vocabulary
findings.description: The measurement level, bounds and favourable direction of any numeric scale, the controlled vocabulary for non-numeric outcomes, and how indeterminate, inapplicable, untested and error states are kept distinct from a negative result.

questions.text: Is the outcome nominal, ordinal, interval or ratio, and what are its bounds?
Which controlled vocabulary expresses non-numeric outcomes for this assessment?
answer_data: Default value where no result is produced

questions.text: Which direction of the scale is favourable, and what are the best and worst attainable values?
How are untested, not-checked, error and not-selected states distinguished from a negative result?
answer_data: Rule forbidding coercion to a negative result
Downstream handling of each indeterminate value

data_elements.name: Scale definition reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the versioned scale definition in effect.

data_elements.name: Worst attainable value
